title: Tag Services
content_html:
Tag Services

Stable Structure

Studio route controller
  -> studio_tags_api.py dispatch by allowlisted path
  -> studio_tag_api/ translates HTTP body/result
  -> studio/services/tags/ validates and plans domain change
  -> tag_write_transactions.py atomic replace
  -> studio/data/canonical/tags/

Reads and writes are served by Local Studio under /studio/api/tags. Endpoint constants in studio/services/tags/tag_routes.py and dispatch maps in studio/app/server/studio/studio_tags_api.py are the exact route inventory.

Ownership

  • tag_source_paths.py — canonical path contract.
  • tag_source_model.py — flat IDs, scalar groups, limits, normalization, schema validation, and registry-backed alias constraints.
  • tag_assignment_service.py — direct series/work assignment save planning.
  • focused registry/alias/promotion mutation modules — cross-file plans and impact summaries.
  • studio_tag_api/ — request parsing and service response shaping.
  • tag_write_transactions.py — atomic single/multi-file replacement and rollback on partial failure.
  • studio_tags_api.py — GET/POST allowlists only.

Mutation Families

  • save series/work assignments;
  • create/edit/delete registry tags;
  • create/edit/delete aliases;
  • promote an alias into a canonical tag;
  • demote a canonical tag into an alias;
  • preview destructive/cross-file effects before apply.

Exact request fields belong to the handlers/tests. The important common contract is: validate IDs and current source, plan effects without writing, then apply through the fixed transaction boundary.

Safety And Failure

  • writes are confined to Registry, Aliases, and Assignments source paths;
  • subprocesses and arbitrary browser paths are not part of this service;
  • multi-file replacements retain original bytes for in-process rollback;
  • dry-run paths return planned effects without canonical writes;
  • failed assignment saves remain unsaved in the current editor and do not create another persistence authority.

Extension Method

Add the narrowest domain function first, then an API wrapper and one allowlisted route. Cover validation, dry-run/no-write, cross-file effects, rollback, and HTTP dispatch at the smallest useful level.

Do not add a generic mutation endpoint or browser-selected source path. If a new workflow changes several canonical files, its service should own one explicit plan and one atomic apply boundary.
